subject: Intermittent stream frame mismatch impacting Cornerstone checkout (urgent)
messages:
From: Kate Rivers <kate@cornerstone-retail.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: eng-team@cornerstone-retail.com
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 14:03:00 -0400
Subject: Checkout failures and 5xxs from Redwood streaming (production)

Rohan,

We started seeing serious failures across our checkout flow this morning when calls are hitting Redwood via the client SDK. Symptoms: p99 token latency jumps from ~120ms to >3s, intermittent 502/504s and a sharp uptick in error-rate (from 0.2% to ~6% over the last 45m). This is live traffic on our us-east-1 Dedicated pool.

Attached is a short extract from our edge logs showing repeated: "stream parse error: incomplete headers at frame boundary" and a few sample request ids. We rolled back to an older SDK (v1.9.2) for a small percentage of traffic and errors dropped significantly, which makes us suspect a client-side change.

Can Redwood take immediate ownership? This is affecting checkout success and we need a mitigation and ETA for a fix. We have a renewal conversation coming up next month so this is urgent.

Thanks,
Kate Rivers
SVP Product, Cornerstone Retail

Attachment: cornerstone_error_sample.log

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
To: Kate Rivers <kate@cornerstone-retail.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 14:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Checkout failures and 5xxs from Redwood streaming (production)

Kate — thanks for the alert and the logs. I’m escalating immediately.

Short plan of action (initial):
- Triage: Vivek/Victor/Hannah to reproduce and identify whether this is client or server.
- Mitigation: temporarily route Cornerstone traffic to the non-streaming fallback and pin to a stable model variant.
- Customer communication: I’ll keep you updated every 2 hours.

Vivek/Hannah: please prioritize and post findings to SUP-3219. If this is a client parser regression we should prepare a hotfix and a clear rollback/migration plan for customers on Dedicated.

—Rohan
Head of Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 15:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Checkout failures and 5xxs from Redwood streaming (production)

Rohan / team — initial triage notes below. I dug into the trace samples (thank you Kate) and reproduced locally against their request patterns.

Observation: when multiple chunked-stream frames arrive coalesced in a single TCP segment, our JS client SDK (v2.3.0) occasionally drops the trailing CRLF between frames under high-concurrency conditions. That causes the streaming parser to interpret the header boundary incorrectly and emit a "incomplete headers" parse error.

Repro steps (attached): rapid-sender test -> coalesce frames -> parser sees "frame boundary shuffle" -> error. I’ve pushed a minimal repro gist and a short trace (SUP-3219).

Immediate mitigation candidate:
- Toggle the client flag enable_chunked_guardrails=false on their SDK to force conservative frame flushing.
- Server-side: enable a tolerant header-reassembly path for their pool that tolerates missing CRLF and waits up to 30ms for trailing bytes.

If we take both steps we should see a quick drop in error-rate; the server-side tolerant path is lower-risk and can be reverted. I’ll prepare a PR and a short test plan for the patch.

Attachment: repro_gist.txt
Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-3219

—Hannah
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 15:37:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Checkout failures and 5xxs from Redwood streaming (production)

Team — thanks for the quick investigation. This is a customer-impacting regression with SLA exposure and renewal risk. Recommendation: prioritize a two-track response immediately:

1) Customer mitigation (hours): implement the client-side toggle and route Cornerstone to the tolerant server reassembly worker. Monitor error-rate and latency for 2-4 hours.
2) Engineering fix (days): prepare a targeted client SDK patch to make the parser robust to coalesced frames, plus a server-side regression test for multiplexed arrivals. Aim for a hotfix release within 48 hours.

I’m looping in Monica for CS/legal coordination on credits and notification. If exec approval is needed for a customer credit and priority engineering resources, flag it now — I recommend we offer a one-month service credit if Cornerstone accepts the temporary patch and we verify recovery.

Vivek
VP, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
To: Kate Rivers <kate@cornerstone-retail.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 09:10:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Checkout failures and 5xxs from Redwood streaming (production)

Kate — quick update and recommended next steps.

Thanks for the logs. Our triage points to an SDK parser regression when frames are coalesced by the network stack. We have two safe mitigations we’d like to apply immediately (with your OK):

1) Client-side toggle (non-breaking): set enable_chunked_guardrails=false in your SDK config. This forces conservative flush boundaries and avoids the parser edge. No downtime; requires a config rollout in your client fleet.
2) Server-side tolerance: we can enable a temporary header-reassembly tolerance on your Dedicated pool in us-east-1 to wait up to 30ms for missing trailing bytes before failing the request. This is reversible and doesn’t change persisted data.

If you approve both we’ll:
- Apply (2) on the Dedicated pool within 30 minutes.
- Share a small rollout plan for (1) and assist with a canary.
- Open SUP-3219 with live metrics and a target hotfix within 48 hours.

We are prepared to offer a one-month credit if we do not achieve recovery within the mitigation window. If you’d prefer, we can also push an emergency client SDK patch to your canary build.

Do you want us to proceed with enabling the server-side tolerance now?

—Rohan

From: Kate Rivers <kate@cornerstone-retail.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: eng-team@cornerstone-retail.com, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 11:22:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Checkout failures and 5xxs from Redwood streaming (production)

Rohan, thanks — please proceed with the server-side tolerance immediately and we’ll roll the client toggle to canary now. We’ll share canary results in 1 hour.

Also copy our procurement and legal (procurement@cornerstone-retail.com) on the credit conversation and include the patch notes for our security review. We appreciate the quick response — please confirm when the Dedicated pool change is live.

Thanks,
Kate
SVP Product, Cornerstone Retail
